questions.question:
**In the following question, one part of the sentence may have an error. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and click the option corresponding to it. If the sentence is free from error, click the "No error" option.**

International Mother Earth Day is celebrated (1)/ every year to remind us that the Earth provides us with life (2)/ and we should be grudgeful for the same. (3)/ No error (4)
questions.solution: The error lies in the third part of the given sentence as one should be ‘grateful’ or thankful to the Earth for all it provides. ‘Grudgeful’ refers to someone who holds bitterness against someone. Thus, option 3 is the correct answer.

questions.question:
**In the following question, one part of the sentence may have an error. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and click the option corresponding to it. If the sentence is free from error, click the "No error" option.**

A shepherd boy (1)/ tended his masters sheep (2)/ near a dark forest not far from the village. (3)/ No error (4)
questions.solution: ‘To tend’ means to look after. The given sentence carries the meaning that the shepherd boy looked after the sheep that *belonged to the master*. Thus the possessive form of master/ masters should be used, i.e., master’s or masters' (if there are more than one masters).

questions.question:
**The sentence(s) given with blanks are to be filled with an appropriate word(s). Four alternatives are suggested for each question. For each question, choose the correct alternative and click the button corresponding to it.**

Her heart was ______ with joy.
questions.solution: ‘Was’ indicates that the action happened in the past, therefore the past form of the word ‘fill’ should be used. Thus option 3 is the correct answer. ‘Fulled’ is grammatically incorrect.

questions.question:
**The sentence(s) given with blanks are to be filled with an appropriate word(s). Four alternatives are suggested for each question. For each question, choose the correct alternative and click the button corresponding to it.**

Abhishek has a bad habit of ______ his car keys.
questions.solution:
Among all the given options, ‘misplacing’ conveys the correct meaning. Thus, **option 2** is the correct answer.

From the sentence, it is evident that a participle would fit the blank. The present participle form of the base form of the verb 'misplace' is 'misplacing' 

It means *putting (an object) in the wrong place and so lose it temporarily*

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, choose the word which best expresses the meaning of the given word and click the button corresponding to it.**

Clamour
questions.solution:
The meanings of some of the words are as follows:

Clamour => a loud and confused noise

Uproar => a loud noise or disturbance

Foresee => predict

Thus, option 3 is the synonym of the given word.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, choose the word which best expresses the meaning of the given word and click the button corresponding to it.**

Quash
questions.solution: ‘Quash’ means to crush or squeeze something. Thus, option 4 is the best fit answer.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, choose the word which best expresses the meaning of the given word and click the button corresponding to it.**

Abandon
questions.solution: ‘Abandon’ means to leave something or no longer take care of it. ‘Forsake’ carries the same meaning, thus option 4 is the correct answer.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, choose the word which is opposite in meaning to the given word and click the button corresponding to it.**

Movement
questions.solution: All the words except ‘static’ show movement. ‘Static’ refers to something that is still and does not move. Thus, option 1 is the correct answer.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, choose the word which is opposite in meaning to the given word and click the button corresponding to it.**

Kindness
questions.solution: ‘Meanness’ is opposite in meaning to kindness, thus, option 1 is the correct answer.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, choose the word which is opposite in meaning to the given word and click the button corresponding to it.**

Recondite
questions.solution:
Let’s look at the meanings of some of the words first:

Recondite => little known, abstract

Occult => mystical, supernatural

Clearly, ‘straight forward’ carries the opposite meaning to ‘recondite’. Options 1 and 3 are its synonyms.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the Idiom/ Phrase.**

Ball is in your court

options.text: It is up to me to make the next decision or step
It is up to you to make the next decision or step

questions.solution: When we say that the *ball is in someone’s court*, it means that it is up to them to make the next decision. Thus, option 2 is the correct answer.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the Idiom/ Phrase.**

Bag and baggage
questions.solution: The idiom ‘bag and baggage’ means ‘with all one’s belongings’. Thus, option 4 is the correct answer.

questions.question:
**Below are three alternatives which may be used to improve the sentence by replacing the words given in the brackets. You may choose option 1, 2 or 3. In case no improvement is needed, choose 4.**

One must (be in the company) a doctor during sickness.
questions.solution: You go to a doctor when you are sick, i.e., you ‘visit’ her. ‘Accompany’ means to go somewhere along with someone. Thus, option 1 is the best fit answer.

questions.question:
**Below are three alternatives which may be used to improve the sentence by replacing the words given in the brackets. You may choose option 1, 2 or 3. In case no improvement is needed, choose 4.**

His father won't be able to leave for Mumbai (until they have arrived).
questions.solution: The first clause of the given sentence talks about an action that will take place in the future. The clause after ‘until’ indicates the condition for it. In a sentence where the main clause is in the future, the subordinate sentence introduced by a time conjunction (when, while, by the time, until, etc.) must remain in the present tense. Thus, option 1 is the correct answer.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which is the best substitute of the phrase.**

One who hoards wealth and spends as little money as possible
questions.solution:
*One who hoards wealth and spends as little money as possible* is known as a miser. Thus, option 3 is the correct answer.

The other options are not synonymous with miser:

 
• Member means a person who belongs to a group or organization.
 
• Macho means behaving or appearing to behave in a way that is stereotypically masculine.
 
• Militant means supporting or engaging in extreme or unyielding methods of achieving political or social goals.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which is the best substitute of the phrase.**

Sudden uncontrollable fear or anxiety, often causing wildly unthinking behaviour.
questions.solution: A *sudden uncontrollable fear or anxiety, often causing wildly unthinking behaviour *is known as anxiety. Thus, option 3 is the correct answer.

questions.question:
**The question below consists of a set of labelled sentences. Out of the four options given, select the most logical order of the sentences to form a coherent sentence.**

Life

P: is a

Q: great

R: teacher
questions.solution: The given part must be followed by P as mentions the verb. Q follows next as has the adjective for the noun ‘teacher’ (that has been mentioned in R).

questions.question:
**The question below consists of a set of labelled sentences. Out of the four options given, select the most logical order of the sentences to form a coherent sentence.**

Parenthood

P: so much joy

Q: gives

R: to people
questions.solution: Q must follow the given part as it tells what ‘parenthood’ does. P should follow next as it states what exactly it gives. R completes the sentence. Thus, QPR is the correct logical order.

questions.question: it's been a _______ journey.
questions.solution: The concerned sentence conveys the meaning that Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam had worked and experienced a lot of things before finally becoming the President of India. Therefore, ‘long’ is the correct adjective to fill the blank space.

questions.question: President Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam talked about life's toughest ________ learnt
questions.solution: You learn lessons and take advices. Thus, option 2 is the best fit answer.

questions.question: his mission _______ a teacher to the Indian youth.
questions.solution: The given sentence means that Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam shared the lessons he learnt in life and his mission *as* a teacher. Thus, ‘being’ (existing as a) should be put in the third blank to convey the appropriate meaning.

questions.question: A proper education would help nurture a sense of _________
questions.solution: Education will obviously result into something positive. Since all the option except ‘dignity’ express negative things, option 1 is the correct answer.

questions.question: Life was _______ mission for President Kalam.
questions.solution: It has been established that Kalam was curious about learning new things about life. Thus it can be said that he treated life like a mission. Since mission is a singular ‘noun’ and has not been already specified, the article ‘a’ should be used before it. ‘Scheduled mission’ is inappropriate in the given context. Thus, option 1 is the best fit answer.
